critical.issue: FIXED: images field was returned as JSON string ('[\'url1\',\'url2\']') instead of a parsed list. build_service() function did not parse the images JSON string back to a list.

integration_issues.issue: CRITICAL: The ownership check in loadServiceForEdit() does not redirect non-owner coaches when the page is directly loaded (via URL/page.goto). Root cause: useEffect([serviceId]) fires immediately on mount when user=null (AuthContext.checkAuth() is still async-loading user from storage). user?.user_id is undefined, condition short-circuits to FALSE, no Alert + no redirect. The backend correctly returns 403 on PUT, but the non-owner can still VIEW and interact with the pre-filled edit form.
integration_issues.reproduction: Login as coach@winek.app (user_coach001), navigate directly to /create-service?serviceId=svc_b184a9f7f6db (service owned by user_demo001) - edit form loads with no redirect

action_items: FIX ownership check timing bug: In create-service.tsx, loadServiceForEdit useEffect depends on [serviceId] but user may be null (auth not loaded). Fix: change useEffect dependency to [serviceId, user?.user_id] or check `if (isEditMode && serviceId && user)` before calling loadServiceForEdit. Alternatively use a ref for user in the async function.

VERIFY: images fix in build_service() is working - all 9 backend tests pass after the fix. This fix is critical as the frontend's loadServiceForEdit parses the images field and needs it as a list, not string.
critical_code_review_comments: BUG FIXED: build_service() in service_routes.py was not parsing JSON string images field to list. Added: if isinstance(raw_images, str): row_dict['images'] = json.loads(raw_images). Pattern similar to _enrich_service's tag_ids parsing.

BUG (main agent action needed): create-service.tsx ownership check in loadServiceForEdit() uses user from closure, but when page is directly loaded (refresh/direct URL), user=null at the time useEffect fires because AuthContext.checkAuth() is still running. Fix: add user as dependency or use AuthContext loading state.

NOTE: svc_b184a9f7f6db is owned by user_demo001 (user@winek.app, role=coach). Both test users have role=coach. The review_request's agent note stating 'user@winek.app has role=user' was incorrect - both accounts have role=coach.

rca_of_issue.bug: Ownership check in create-service.tsx does not redirect on direct page load
rca_of_issue.root_cause: Backend logs confirm /api/auth/me is called and completes BEFORE /api/services/{id}, so user state IS loaded when loadServiceForEdit runs. The condition (data.coach_id !== user.user_id) evaluates to TRUE and Alert.alert is called. However: (1) React Native Web Alert.alert renders as a custom modal (not window.alert), so Playwright's page.on('dialog') cannot capture it. (2) router.back() fails silently when page is directly loaded (no browser history entry). There is NO fallback route when canGoBack()=false, unlike the role check which uses: if (router.canGoBack()) router.back(); else router.replace('/(tabs)/profile').
rca_of_issue.reproduction: Login as coach@winek.app, then directly navigate to /create-service?serviceId=svc_b184a9f7f6db. Alert.alert is likely called but invisible (RN custom modal). router.back() fails silently (no history). Edit form stays open.
rca_of_issue.mitigation: In loadServiceForEdit ownership check, replace router.back() with the same pattern as the role check: setTimeout(() => { if (router.canGoBack()) router.back(); else router.replace('/(tabs)/profile' as any); }, 100). This ensures redirect even when page is loaded directly.
